title: Bell and Visitor
premise: Petra Okafor returns to the isolated village of Hollowmere to bury his twin sister Ada, who died there under circumstances no one will explain. On his first night, a church bell that was melted down in 1911 begins to ring, and with each toll the villagers' faces change, revealing they have been keeping something fed for generations. Petra learns Ada discovered the truth: the village's founding families invited 'the Visitor' in 1911, trading one villager per generation for protection, and the bell rings when it comes to collect. Refusing to let the Visitor take him as it took Ada, Petra must survive until sunrise by uncovering what was truly invited in—only to learn the Visitor is not the monster; the bargain is, and ending it means burning down everything he came home to love.
about_author: Sebastian Dunmore is the pen name of a former parish archivist who spent a decade cataloguing church records across rural England before turning to fiction. His work is known for quiet dread rooted in bureaucratic horror—the contracts, ledgers, and small-town complicity behind the supernatural.

chapters.title: The Wrong Grave
chapters.summary: Petra arrives in Hollowmere for Ada's funeral, POV his throughout the book. The coffin is closed; the vicar rushes the service; villagers watch him like an intruder. He notices fresh earth beside Ada's plot—an empty grave waiting. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion that no one will name what killed her.

chapters.title: A Bell That Isn't There
chapters.summary: At midnight, Petra hears the church bell ring nine times, though the tower has been empty since 1911. He finds the belfry door chained from outside, rusted shut. In the morning, villagers deny hearing anything, but their hands tremble. Beat: isolation begins; his disbelief meets their practiced denial.

chapters.title: Ada's Ledger
chapters.summary: Searching Ada's cottage, Petra finds her hidden notebook: names, dates, and payments recorded back generations, ending with her own name circled. A neighbor, Mrs. Ellery, warns him to leave before the next full dark. Beat: the horror becomes documentary—his sister knew, and stayed anyway.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Petra breaks into the parish archive and reads the 1911 covenant: the founding families formally 'invited in' the Visitor after a famine, pledging one soul per generation. The melted bell was recast into the covenant itself. Beat: dread deepens as he realizes the ritual is legalistic, binding, and still active.

chapters.title: Nine Tolling
chapters.summary: The bell rings again—this time at dusk, and everyone hears it. Villagers gather in the square, faces slack, and Petra watches them choose among themselves who will stand at the churchyard gate tonight. Beat: terror of complicity; the community's love for each other is built on sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Gate
chapters.summary: Petra follows the chosen man, old Tom Wren, to the gate and witnesses the Visitor: a figure shaped like whoever you grieve most—for Petra, Ada herself. Tom walks through willingly. Petra flees before it sees him. Beat: heartbreak weaponized; the Visitor wears love as a lure.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Mrs. Ellery confesses she raised Ada to be the offering, believing duty outweighed blood. Petra rages, then finds Ada's final letter: she went willingly to buy Petra time, knowing he'd come. Beat: grief reframed as inheritance—Ada left him a choice, not just a warning.

chapters.title: Reading the Covenant Backwards
chapters.summary: Petra discovers the covenant's flaw: it binds only those who acknowledge it. Belief is the signature. If no heir accepts the debt, the invitation lapses—but the Visitor will claim the whole village first. Beat: rising tension; survival now requires unbelief held under impossible pressure until dawn.

chapters.title: Sunrise Clause
chapters.summary: Climax. The bell tolls without stopping. The Visitor comes for Petra wearing Ada's voice, offering her return if he signs. Through the longest night he refuses—grieving, tempted, holding out as villagers are taken around him. At first light he speaks the renunciation aloud. Beat: love tested against duty, and love winning by letting go.

chapters.title: Bell and Visitor
chapters.summary: Resolution. The bell falls silent forever; the tower crumbles. Half the village is gone, and the survivors must live with what they did. Petra buries Ada properly in the second grave—empty after all—and leaves without looking back, carrying her ledger so no one forgets. Beat: survival's price paid; inheritance transformed into witness.
